title: Minimum Absolute Value Approach for Ambitious Kid
approach_explanation: The problem asks for the minimum number of operations to make the product of an array equal to zero. The product of a set of numbers is zero if and only if at least one of the numbers is zero. Therefore, we can achieve a product of zero by choosing a single element and changing its value to zero. The number of operations required to change an element $A_i$ to $0$ is precisely its absolute value $|A_i|$, since we can increment or decrement it by $1$ in each step. To minimize the total operations, we only need to pick the element that is closest to zero initially—that is, the element with the minimum absolute value across the entire array.

code_breakdown.explanation: Read the size of the array $n$ and initialize a variable `abs_minimum` to `INT_MAX` to store the minimum absolute value encountered so far.

code_breakdown.section_title: Iterating and Finding the Minimum Absolute Value
code_breakdown.explanation: Loop through all $n$ input elements. For each number, compute its absolute value using `abs(num)` and update `abs_minimum` if the current absolute value is smaller than the recorded minimum.
Print the final `abs_minimum`, representing the minimum operations needed to bring at least one element to zero.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: The solution iterates through the array of size $N$ exactly once. Inside the loop, all operations (reading input, computing absolute value, comparison) take $O(1)$ time, resulting in a linear time complexity of $O(N)$.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: The algorithm processes inputs on-the-fly and only uses a few scalar integer variables (`n`, `abs_minimum`, `num`, `i`), requiring constant auxiliary space beyond the input stream.

strengths: Optimal time and space complexity with single-pass processing.
Properly utilizes standard library functions like `abs` and `INT_MAX`.
